description: Binding lifecycle and recovery policy for Memory OS PostgreSQL schema changes. Transaction rollback is not treated as migration rollback completion. Additive expansion and forward-fix are the defaults; destructive contraction requires separate evidence and approval.

requiredEvidence: available recovery point and restore owner
old and new application version compatibility statement
phases.exitCriteria: all required evidence recorded; no ambiguity about target, recovery point or compatibility

allowed: add tables and indexes without removing old paths
add compatible functions, policies and constraints in non-enforcing form
forbidden: drop columns or tables still read by any deployed version
rename a required surface without a compatibility bridge
rewrite a large table inside an unbounded deployment transaction
silently weaken FORCE RLS or deployment-role isolation
phases.exitCriteria: old and new application versions can both operate against the expanded schema

allowed: pause and resume without deleting ambiguous state
forbidden: unbounded one-shot backfill coupled to application deployment
marking incomplete rows complete to clear an alert
phases.exitCriteria: backfill accounting is complete and independently verified

requiredEvidence: old and new version traffic observed
no migration-specific alert or lock backlog
phases.exitCriteria: defined observation window completed with no unresolved integrity or compatibility issue

allowed: remove compatibility surfaces only after old-version drain
remove deprecated data only after retention and recovery review
forbidden: contract while an old application version can still run
contract without an isolated recovery point
phases.exitCriteria: deprecated surfaces removed deliberately and post-contract verification completed

readiness.note: The lifecycle policy and runbook are foundations only. A clean-database dry run, mixed-version proof, recovery-point integration, evidence ledger and production-shaped rehearsal remain required, so OPS-P0-001 stays PARTIAL.
